interest: Tax status of foreign state-enterprise staff in the U.S., including Japanese officials, between the wars.
keywords: Agents of Japan in the United States
overview: This file comprises nine pages of the Department of State's docket list (List of Papers) for decimal file 894.01 B 11 ('Agents of Japan in the United States'), spanning correspondence from September 1934 through June 1936. The entries record extensive diplomatic negotiations and inter-agency deliberations among the Japanese Embassy, the Department of State, and the Treasury Department concerning the federal income tax liability of non-diplomatic Japanese officials and commercial agents stationed in the United States, particularly representatives of the Imperial Japanese Government Railways. The dispute was initiated when internal revenue officers in New York demanded income tax payments and surety bonds from departing railway officials such as Yorio Yamamoto, prompting bilateral efforts to establish tax exemption on the basis of reciprocity. Following the introduction and passage of H.R. 7998 by Congress, the State Department and Treasury certified reciprocal exemptions, instructed collectors of internal revenue at major ports to grant sailing permits without hindrance, adjudicated the status of quasi-governmental agencies like the Board of Tourist Industry, and arranged for the refund of taxes paid and the cancellation of deposited surety bonds.

subfiles.about: Department of State docket list (List of Papers) recording diplomatic notes, Treasury rulings, and departmental memoranda concerning the income tax liability and reciprocal exemption of Japanese government officials and commercial agents in the United States from September 1934 to June 1936.
keywords: Agents of Japan in the United States
subfiles.summary: This nine-page docket register (List of Papers) chronicles communications exchanged between the Japanese Embassy, the Department of State, and the Treasury Department regarding the federal income tax status of Japanese government personnel and commercial agents stationed in the United States. Originating with demands by New York revenue authorities that departing Japanese railway official Yorio Yamamoto pay back taxes, the docket follows the posting of surety bonds for various Japanese agents and the introduction in Congress of H.R. 7998 to establish reciprocal tax immunity for non-diplomatic foreign government employees. It documents inter-departmental legal opinions, deliberations over proposed bilateral exchanges of notes, certification of reciprocity by Acting Secretary Phillips, and the transmission of instructions to collectors of internal revenue at New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Seattle. Later entries detail the resolution of individual claims, including the exemption of named railway representatives, the clarification of the status of the Board of Tourist Industry versus the private Japan Tourist Bureau, the visit of Financial Commissioner Yutaro Tomita, and the eventual refunding of taxes paid and cancellation of surety bonds.
